answer: Sybil resistance is a scarce admission queue. Each identity burns a small timber fee to reserve a validation slot, then must keep a live work-ember — a rolling hash of peer-attested, non-repeating tasks — hot across K consecutive checkpoints. Letting the ember cool, or reusing another seat's task graph, evicts the identity and forfeits the fee. Epoch zenith capacity is fixed, and one custody root may heat only one ember, so cheap clones cannot multiply slots.
